title: Baklava
subtitle: Layered filo pastry with nuts and honey syrup
excerpt: Crisp layers of buttered filo pastry filled with a spiced mixture of finely chopped walnuts and pistachios, baked until shatteringly golden, then drenched in a hot syrup of honey, lemon, and orange blossom water. Made in a large tray and cut into diamonds.

recipe.sourceNotes: Baklava is eaten across the Middle East, Turkey, the Balkans, and Central Asia, with all regions claiming some form of ownership. The Ottoman court kitchen at the Topkapı Palace in Istanbul is often credited with developing the modern layered filo version, which spread across the Ottoman Empire and beyond. Turkish and Middle Eastern versions differ primarily in the nut filling (pistachios for Turkish and Levantine versions, walnuts for Balkan and Greek versions) and the syrup (simple sugar syrup for Turkish, honey-heavy for Greek and Levantine). The technique is the same across all versions: layers of filo brushed with clarified butter or ghee, with the nut filling in the centre, cut before baking into diamond or square shapes so the syrup penetrates to every layer.

content.text: The syrup must be poured hot over the hot baklava, or cold over cold; never mix the temperatures or the pastry will become soggy. Cut through all the layers completely before baking; attempting to cut the baked baklava will shatter it. Keep the filo sheets covered with a damp cloth while you work to prevent them drying out.

items.preparation: or walnuts, pistachios, or a mixture; finely chopped but not ground

content.text: Heat the oven to 180°C / fan 160°C / gas 4. Mix the chopped nuts with the 30 g sugar and cinnamon. Brush a 30 x 22 cm baking tin with clarified butter. Layer 10 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each sheet generously with butter and trimming to fit.

Spread the nut mixture evenly over the filo. Layer 10 more sheets of filo on top, brushing each with butter. Using a sharp knife, cut the baklava all the way through to the base in diagonal lines to form diamond shapes. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

While the baklava bakes, make the syrup: combine the 150 g sugar, honey, lemon juice, cinnamon stick, and 150 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove the cinnamon. Pour the hot syrup over the hot baklava immediately it comes out of the oven. Leave to soak for at least 2 hours before serving.
